title: Gates that must fail their negative control
summary: Drake trusts a gate only after it fails on something broken on purpose. In this lesson an Omega gate checks that SI's real install.sh pins one explicit release and never 'latest'; it passes the real file and fails two sed mutants. A weaker gate that only looks for a TAG= line passes the mutants too, so it is refused as a gate. I can help you add a negative control to any check, and I will remind you that a host gate is not hardware qualification.
goal: Write a gate that accepts the real input, rejects a mutated one, and refuse any gate that cannot tell them apart.
key_steps: State what the gate guards in one sentence
Run it on the real input and expect exit 0
Make mutants that break exactly the guarded property
Require a nonzero exit on every mutant in the same script
Refuse the gate if any negative control is accepted
Say what the gate does not cover, and that a host gate is not hardware qualification

example.code:
note pingate: an installer script on stdin must install one explicit release, never "latest"
note PASS needs exactly one line TAG=value with value not empty and not latest, and no releases/latest URL
note exit 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 4 REFUSED (input too big or unreadable)
text ttag "TAG="
text tlatest "latest "
text turl "releases/latest"
text tlines "TAG lines "
text tval "TAG value "
text tnone "(none)"
text turls "releases/latest URLs "
text vpass "verdict PASS\n"
text vfail "verdict FAIL\n"
text nl "\n"
note g: 0 TAG lines, 1 bad TAG values, 2 latest URLs, 3 start of the first TAG value, 4 its end
global g ulong 5
fn oneline a ulong b ulong to void
if lt add a 4 b
if sameb ttag 0 a 4
c = get g 0
if eq c 0
put g 3 add a 4
put g 4 b
end
put g 0 add c 1
k = lookup tlatest add a 4 b
if ge k 0
put g 1 add get g 1 1
end
end
end
end
fn urls n ulong to void
for i ulong n
if sameb turl 0 i len turl
put g 2 add get g 2 1
end
end
end
fn main to int
r = rdall
if lt r 0
ret 4
end
if eq get st 2 1
ret 4
end
n = ulong r
a = ulong 0
for i ulong n
if eq get inb i 10
oneline a i
a = add i 1
end
end
oneline a n
urls n
ot tlines
on get g 0
ot nl
ot tval
if gt get g 0 0
oi get g 3 get g 4
else
ot tnone
end
ot nl
ot turls
on get g 2
ot nl
v = int 1
if eq get g 0 1
if eq add get g 1 get g 2 0
v = 0
end
end
if eq v 0
ot vpass
else
ot vfail
end
f = flush
ret v
end

common_mistake: Seeing a gate pass on good input and stopping; a gate that always exits 0 does that too. Run the negative control every time. Never loosen a gate until the current code passes.

evidence_note: Both gates ran on install.sh at the pinned SI commit and on two mutants on a Linux arm64 host. pingate rejected both mutants; pingate_weak accepted them and was refused. Host-only; says nothing about the download, signature or bundle.
